name: Peter
bio:
Simon, called Peter, was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee when Jesus called him and his brother Andrew to follow him and become "fishers of men"; they immediately left their nets to do so (Matthew 4:18-20). His prominent, often impulsive role among the disciples is told in detail in the chapters ahead. Luke's account adds that this call came after Jesus taught from Peter's boat and then told him, despite a fruitless night of fishing, to let down his nets again; the catch was so great it nearly sank both boats, and Peter, astonished, fell at Jesus's knees crying, "Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord," before Jesus reassured him and he left everything to follow (Luke 5:1-11). When Jesus entered Peter's house, he healed Peter's mother-in-law of a fever with a touch (Matthew 8:14-15). When Jesus walked on the water during a storm, Peter asked to join him and briefly walked on the water himself, but began to sink when fear overtook his faith; Jesus caught him and gently rebuked his doubt (Matthew 14:28-31). When the disciples asked for clarification on Jesus's teaching that defilement comes from the heart rather than food, Peter was the one who asked him to explain the saying (Matthew 15:15-20).

 At Caesarea Philippi, when Jesus asked who the disciples believed he was, Peter declared him "the Christ, the Son of the living God"; Jesus blessed him for this Father-given revelation, declared he would build his church on this foundation, and gave him the keys of the kingdom of heaven. When Jesus then predicted his own coming death in Jerusalem, Peter rebuked him for it, and Jesus sharply called him "Satan" for thinking only in human terms (Matthew 16:13-23).

 Peter witnessed Jesus's transfiguration with Moses and Elijah, offering to build shelters for them before a voice from heaven interrupted. Later, when Capernaum's tax collectors questioned him about the temple tax, Jesus had him catch a fish with a coin in its mouth to pay it for them both (Matthew 17:1-27). Peter asked Jesus how many times he should forgive a repeatedly sinning brother, suggesting seven; Jesus answered "seventy times seven," teaching boundless forgiveness (Matthew 18:21-22). Peter asked Jesus what reward the disciples would receive for having given up everything to follow him; Jesus promised them thrones in the age to come, and that the last would be first (Matthew 19:27-30).

 At the Last Supper, Peter confidently insisted he would never desert Jesus even if everyone else did, but Jesus predicted he would deny him three times before dawn. At Gethsemane, Peter was among the three disciples Jesus took deeper into the garden, though he fell asleep each time Jesus checked on them. After Jesus's arrest, Peter followed at a distance into the high priest's courtyard, but when questioned three times about his association with Jesus, he denied knowing him each time, growing more emphatic with each denial; when the rooster crowed as predicted, Peter remembered Jesus's words and wept bitterly (Matthew 26:33-75).
